# R421 — Prefill residual capture for multi-position teacher-forced scoring

Date: 2026-10-13. Source-only semantic audit of fixed P/4K. No implementation, execution, test, build, lint, AST, GPU, profiler, cleanup, process/service, or active candidate inspection.

## Finding

A single fresh layer-major prefill can expose up to 64 final-layer FP32 residual rows at selected global positions through the existing `Prefill::on_chunk` callback. One row is 10240 floats / 40960 bytes, so 64 rows cost 2,621,440 bytes (2.5 MiB). The source path processes all chunks while uploading each expert layer once for that request. Copying selected rows into independent host-owned storage during the final-layer callback, then scoring them only after the phase prompt lifecycle has retired the private prefill workspace and restored the decode cache/head, is a plausible way to score many teacher-forced positions without repeating a fresh GEN1 first-row request for each position.

That is a source-level feasibility result, not a quality or performance result. It can provide a controlled multi-position baseline for the exact FP32 residuals produced by one P/4K run and can screen the *local* effect of rounding those final residual rows to FP16/BF16 before the head. It does not simulate the accumulated error from transporting rounded residuals between every pair of model layers: a final-layer capture has no downstream layers left to propagate such error through. A true inter-layer FP16/BF16 transport candidate still needs its own bounded full traversal or layer-boundary controlled harness. No adoption is decided here; Main can decide after current measurements.

The result must use a new explicit fixed-history/multi-row producer and schema. It cannot reuse the strict `serve-first-row` verifier adapter by writing invented metadata: the existing producer is one first verifier row at `prompt_P-1`, effective T=1, fresh `max_new=1`, then one emitted token. A Prefill capture has multiple FP32 residual rows indexed by global input position and has different lifetimes, inputs, and scoring semantics.

## Producer and capture semantics

In fixed P/4K, `Prefill::run()` dispatches to `run_layer_major()` when requested. `run_layer_major()` walks layers in ascending order and runs all prompt chunks for one layer before the next. Its per-layer `on_chunk` wrapper sends residual output to the caller only for the final model layer. The underlying `run_impl()` reaches the callback after a checked compute-stream synchronization; the phase wrapper adds the actual chunk admission check and preserves the preexisting callback. Thus at a callback for `(rows,count,p0)`, the rows are final-layer output residuals for global input positions `[p0,p0+count)`, ready to copy. They are not an output-head mixed vector or logits.

For capture, select a fixed, sorted, unique list of at most 64 positions before starting the request. Validate `0 <= p < n_input`, that each target `tokens[p+1]` is present when an NLL label is required, and that positions are inside the exact admitted request extent. For each selected `p` in the callback interval, copy exactly `D*sizeof(float)` bytes from `rows + (p-p0)*D` into an independent owned FP32 buffer and record the canonical global position and label `tokens[p+1]`. Copy before returning from the callback: `rows` belongs to the Prefill workspace and is reused by the next chunk. Do not retain its pointer, a view into the bridge, or a pointer to the private cache.

A host vector for the selected FP32 rows is independent of the phase workspace and survives the later owner transition. At the maximum capture count its payload is 2.5 MiB. If an asynchronous device-to-host copy is used, its destination must be owned/pinned for that transfer and its completion checked before callback return or before any owner teardown; a plain blocking checked copy inside the callback is easier to reason about. After lifecycle restoration, copy one row at a time into a dedicated device residual scratch, form the exact head input, and reuse one full-vocabulary logits buffer. `NativeHead::run()` requires a loaded head, device input/output buffers, and an explicit stream. Do not pass the former Prefill `rows` pointer to it after the callback.

The maximum full-vocabulary output is 248320 FP32 values = 993280 bytes per row, or 63,569,920 bytes (about 60.6 MiB) for 64 full rows. If the consumer needs only NLL and a few rank statistics, process/read each full row in turn and retain compact per-position scores and provenance rather than a duplicate raw logits corpus. NLL needs the full-vocabulary log-sum-exp, even when only the labelled token score is retained.

## Final head path and phase-owner safety

`NativeHead::run()` is the output projection only. The established single-token `run_head` path first calls `lm_head_mix()`, then `NativeHead::run()`. For this model, `lm_head_mix()` applies the output hyper-connection read (`output_hc_norm`, `output_hc_down`, `output_hc_up`) to the final residual and produces `mixed`; the native head then applies its quantized projection to `output.weight`. This is the existing head path to reproduce for each captured row. Do not treat the raw Prefill residual as `NativeHead::run()` input, and do not omit the output-HC transform. Conversely, avoid introducing an unrelated alternate norm.

The phase code retires verifier/token/session readers before releasing the native head for Prefill, then the successful prompt transition drains/retires the Prefill workspace (`sp.reset()`), restores/publishes the 144-slot baseline and 912-slot decode expert cache, and reloads the native head. Only after those transitions succeed may the diagnostic use `NativeHead::run()`. Keep capture rows in a request-owned buffer that is not tied to `sp`, phase cache extents, bridge storage, or the temporarily released head. Use a dedicated device scratch for one captured row and serialize head runs on an explicit stream. Check launch and sync/readback errors, require all requested logits finite, and retire every reader before the head or scratch can be released. Existing phase fatal/poison behavior applies on uncertain asynchronous work; no result file should be marked complete after a failed copy, head launch, drain, cache publish, or head reload.

This does not make the Prefill callback an API for a `Verifier` row. The producer should explicitly identify itself, e.g. `prefill-final-residual-capture-v1`, with fields for model/tokenizer/input hashes, binary/source/runtime, request extent, chunk/phase geometry, `D`, `float32` row encoding, sorted unique global positions, target token IDs and prediction convention (`R[p]` predicts token `p+1`), number of rows, finite/check status, phase lifecycle receipt, head provider, logits producer, and successful close/reap. Adapter code should reject wrong row order, duplicates, missing positions, payload-size mismatch, target mismatch, nonfinite values, truncated files, unfinished owner receipt, and a claimed row whose producer is `serve-first-row`. Register a new reviewed producer only after an actual controlled capture; keep production/quality flags false before then.

## Causal teacher forcing and remaining numerical uncertainty

There is no evident future-token leak in the inspected batch operators, but equivalence to a one-token causal reference is not yet established for all rows:

- GDN convolution walks each chunk in token order, carrying the prior three QKV values, and commits the final three values after processing the chunk. GDN recurrence loops `t=0..T-1`, applying each row to recurrent state before moving to the next. Each output row is formed from that row's gate/value and the state after its own recurrence step. This is structurally causal; the final source row is not computed from later chunk rows.
- QSA builds `steps` for each row from its absolute `p0+t`, with `n_kv=pos+1`, `n_bid=floor(n_kv/4)`, and the capped selection width. The batch indexer can append several block keys before it scores queries, but `qsa_block_scores` returns for `b > that query's n_bid`; for `b==n_bid` it uses the constant cell-0 `dead` key, not a future block key. `qsa_block_topk` weights full prior blocks and only the current query's partial cells (`n_kv - 4*n_bid`) before emitting cell IDs. This source structure excludes future cells from each query's selected set. `qsa_prompt_attn_batch` consumes those per-query IDs; it is explicitly not bitwise equal to `qsa_decode_attn_batch`, and existing parity bounds are not a full-model teacher-forced equivalence result.
- PLE n-gram rows are gathered from each current token and its preceding pair; that pair advances in input order. At layer 1, each row's `ple_block` runs before `ple_history_advance`, so later history does not feed an earlier row. The layer-major wrapper resets `ple_prev` to the request's original pair before each layer pass, preserving the same starting history rather than carrying the last pair from a prior layer pass.

The ordinary server deliberately pre-fills `n_prompt-1` rows and processes the final prompt token through the first one-token Verifier window. Therefore its first sampled/captured verifier logits predict the token after prompt position `P-1`, whereas a final-layer Prefill residual row at `p` predicts the teacher-forced next token at `p+1`. Rows from ordinary Prefill positions through `P-2` can score prompt-internal next-token labels. To score the first new-token label from a prefill-only diagnostic, the request must explicitly include the final prompt token as a teacher-forced prefill input and capture position `P-1`; this differs from the ordinary GEN split and must be recorded. For multiple continuation labels, the producer must include the needed fixed follow tokens in its input and capture the preceding rows. Do not claim that one captured row at position `P-1` is a first-verifier row without a paired test.

Even with the causal structure, final residuals may differ numerically from one-token Verifier outputs because Prefill uses batched GDN/QSA/Piecewise PLE paths; QSA prompt attention has a different kernel/reduction route from the decode verifier; GDN and MoE matmuls/activation paths may use different batch kernels; and the head mix/projection should be run through the same exact source/provider. Therefore the candidate is valid for measuring the outputs of its own batched FP32 producer, not automatically a faithful substitute for ordinary Verifier logits.

## Minimal comparison plan before any quality claim

Use a small controlled device comparison with an independently produced ordinary single-token causal reference, plus a CPU schema fixture. Keep this separate from the active hardware run.

1. In one fixed prompt, select a few rows including initial PLE positions, QSA block-tail/completion boundaries (`p=0..4` and around `p=2047..2052`), a 4K chunk edge (`4095/4096` when present), a middle position, and a final prompt position only when its next-token label is explicitly supplied. Capture all selected FP32 residual rows in one Prefill run. Compute full-vocabulary logits/NLL with the output-HC mix plus NativeHead path; persist compact per-row evidence and exact token/position labels.
2. For the same token histories and selected positions, independently obtain the reference row by running the ordinary causal path through each position with the same weights/config, using reset/replay or a small dedicated harness. Compare full FP32 logits (finite status, max/mean absolute and relative errors, top-1/top-2, target rank/margin, target NLL). Pre-register tolerances. Include short contexts at which both routes are available; do not treat synthetic fixtures as model evidence.
3. For a *head-only transport screening*, round-trip each saved FP32 final residual through IEEE FP16 or BF16 and back to FP32, apply the same output-HC mix and head projection, and compare per-position logits/NLL with the unrounded captures. Label the scope `final-residual-to-head only`. This costs no expert layer uploads after capture and says nothing about error propagation at earlier layer boundaries.
4. For an actual cross-layer RAM transport claim, create a paired full prefill arm that rounds/de-rounds at every intended inter-layer boundary and compares with the unchanged FP32 arm on the same fixed token histories. At least one run per format is needed; final-row replay alone cannot predict cumulative effects. Capture selected boundaries/positions in one traversal per arm rather than many GEN1 requests, and preserve identical model/runtime/environment and lifecycle. Adoption remains pending measured evidence.
5. CPU negative fixtures should validate the explicit producer schema, global-position to next-label mapping, canonical sorted unique row indexes, format and byte geometry, finite flags, exact file lengths/hashes, provenance, and adapter rejection of forged serve-first-row metadata. They do not validate GPU numerics or producer semantics.

This plan is intentionally bounded and is not a proof of general model capability, all-prefix equivalence, whole-context quality, or all-262144-position behavior. The proposed multi-position NLL diagnostic is optional and is not needed for the current FP32 optimization.

## Existing evidence and registry

The fixed-history numerical capture review R406 reports the existing serve-first-row qualification: fresh 1024 and 32768 requests, one finite FP32 full-vocabulary verifier row at `P-1`, effective `T=1`, no reuse, one emitted token and normal close; row argmax matched the engine's own emitted token. R406 explicitly says this is self-consistency only and not a baseline distribution comparison, fixed-history NLL, layer-major qualification, full context, or RESTORE evidence. Its fixed-history comparator has no reviewed production adapter for this Prefill producer. No numerical run is claimed by R421.

Registry consulted: `/home/yayoi/ghq/github.com/yqYo1/Strata/.worktree/feat-restore-layer-major-prefill-20261013/bench/results/2026-10-13-restored-layer-major-lifecycle/report-registry-v195.json`, SHA-256 `4795eb31f1e100de62148edc73ec4f7bccafd3a5c3262247c0ece442f7245b76`.
